Engine Nodes and State Stores

Engine nodes are the workers of the TaktX engine. They run as Kafka Streams applications, consuming messages from topics, processing them, and managing process state. Let’s look at how they work and how state is managed.

Stateless by Design

Engine nodes themselves are stateless—they don’t keep any long-term data in memory or on disk. Instead, all state is managed in Kafka Streams state stores, which are partitioned and distributed across the cluster. This design makes it easy to scale up and to recover from failures.

State Stores: The Engine’s Memory

Each engine node maintains local state stores for process instances, variables, timers, and message subscriptions. These stores can be configured for in-memory (fast, volatile) or persisted (durable, larger) storage. When a node processes an event, it loads only the relevant state from its local store, keeping memory usage low and performance high.

Partition Assignment

Kafka assigns partitions to engine nodes, ensuring that each node is responsible for a subset of the data. This partitioning is what enables horizontal scaling: as you add more nodes, Kafka redistributes partitions to balance the load.

Recovery and Resilience

If a node fails, Kafka Streams restores its state from the changelog topic. This makes the system highly resilient and minimizes downtime.
